purpose: Define candidate-bound whole-body anatomical attachment and shared-tissue dependencies so movement of one skeletal segment produces coherent deformation in every connected surface region without dragging unrelated tissue.
global_invariants: A shared tissue system is governed by all relevant attachment sides; it may not be owned wholesale by one moving bone.
Proximal and distal attachment neighborhoods remain continuous with their anatomical anchors throughout motion.
Influence transitions between anchors must be spatially gradual; abrupt weight ownership boundaries that create shelves, trenches, membranes or pinches fail.
Lengthening and compression must propagate through the complete connected surface path rather than appearing only at one endpoint.
Volume may redistribute but may not disappear, balloon abruptly or teleport from one attachment side to the other.
Folds arise from compression and relax on unloading/return; persistent fixed creases without mechanical cause fail.
Corrective layers may refine a plausible weights-only path but may not conceal an anatomically wrong attachment/ownership foundation.
Return motion must restore the neutral surface within declared tolerance without residual twist, dent, lobe or offset.
Symmetric skeletal inputs require equivalent left/right coupling absent an explicitly asymmetric task.
Contact/load changes at the hand or foot must propagate through the connected wrist/forearm or ankle/calf chain without local collapse.

coupling_systems.name: cervical_to_trapezius_shoulder_girdle
must_move: neck surface follows distributed cervical motion rather than one rigid hinge
trapezius/neck-to-shoulder slope responds to scapular/clavicular motion
posterior shoulder-girdle surface changes continuously through arm elevation
must_remain_rooted: midline cervical/thoracic attachment remains continuous with trunk
shoulder end remains coupled to clavicle/scapular landmarks

coupling_systems.name: pectoralis_major_anterior_axillary_chain
must_move: humeral insertion side travels with upper arm
anterior axillary fold changes angle/length with arm elevation and rotation
lateral pectoral surface lengthens/shortens smoothly between chest and humerus
must_remain_rooted: central and medial pectoral mass remains chest-rooted
sternal/rib/clavicular chest wall continuity remains stable
forbidden_failures: whole lateral chest dragged with humerus
central pec balloon with lateral collapse

coupling_systems.name: latissimus_teres_posterior_axillary_chain
must_move: posterior axillary fold changes shape with humeral elevation
lat/teres support follows both trunk and humeral attachment sides
posterior chest/back drape changes continuously with scapular contribution
must_remain_rooted: broad posterior trunk mass remains trunk-rooted
distal fold remains connected to humeral insertion side
forbidden_failures: entire lat surface translating with arm

coupling_systems.name: deltoid_shoulder_yoke
must_move: anterior/middle/posterior deltoid surface changes with motion plane
cap remains coupled to both shoulder girdle and humerus
upper-arm transition broadens/narrows continuously rather than stepping

coupling_systems.name: upperarm_elbow_multi_joint_chain
must_move: upper-arm contour responds to elbow flexion/extension without losing shoulder continuity
elbow crease appears under compression and releases under extension
forearm rotation may change distal surface orientation without twisting the upper arm skin as a rigid sleeve

coupling_systems.name: forearm_wrist_hand_load_chain
must_move: forearm rotation changes wrist/palm orientation through a continuous load path
loaded wrist extension compresses/changes the wrist surface without collapsing it
equipment/floor force remains visually continuous into forearm
must_remain_rooted: wrist remains centered between forearm and hand
hand contact does not detach from forearm load path
forbidden_failures: forearm remains visually frozen while palm rotates

coupling_systems.name: finger_flexor_tendon_and_skin_chain
must_move: MCP/PIP/DIP do not use an identical copied curve
volar finger/palm surface follows tendon-guided flexion without bowstring-like detachment
thumb opposition/release is coordinated separately from four-finger flexion
must_remain_rooted: tendon/palm path remains close to finger skeleton
forbidden_failures: thumb behaves as fifth identical finger

coupling_systems.name: ribcage_abdominal_lumbar_pelvic_cylinder
must_move: motion distributes across spinal and pelvic contributors rather than one waist hinge
compressed side forms reversible soft folds while lengthened side remains continuous
ribcage-to-pelvis volume changes gradually through flexion/extension/rotation
must_remain_rooted: ribcage surface remains tied to thorax
pelvic/iliac surface remains tied to pelvis

coupling_systems.name: glute_pelvis_femur_lateral_thigh_chain
must_move: gluteal mass lengthens/reshapes in hip flexion and shortens/reshapes in extension
lateral thigh tension/transition changes with hip ab/adduction and load
pelvis-to-femur connection remains continuous through deep flexion
forbidden_failures: buttock mass sliding wholesale with femur

coupling_systems.name: pelvic_adductor_groin_thigh_chain
must_move: groin/adductor surface lengthens with abduction and compresses with adduction/flexion as appropriate
medial thigh remains continuous with pelvis through deep hip motion
compression folds resolve on return

coupling_systems.name: quadriceps_rectus_patella_chain
must_move: anterior thigh length state responds to knee flexion/extension
rectus femoris response reflects both hip and knee state
quadriceps-to-patella surface/tendon path remains continuous through deep flexion
forbidden_failures: anterior thigh rigid during knee flexion
rectus response driven by knee alone

coupling_systems.name: hamstring_pelvis_thigh_popliteal_chain
must_move: posterior-thigh form responds to combined hip and knee configuration
distal hamstring boundaries change naturally around the popliteal region
hip flexion plus knee extension produces a visibly lengthened chain relative to shortened configurations
forbidden_failures: posterior thigh fixed while both joints change

coupling_systems.name: gastrocnemius_soleus_Achilles_calcaneus_chain
must_move: calf/Achilles shape responds to ankle dorsiflexion/plantarflexion
gastrocnemius component also responds to knee state
Achilles remains a continuous force path to calcaneus during heel rise and return
forbidden_failures: ankle-only solution ignores knee effect on gastrocnemius

coupling_systems.name: ankle_hindfoot_arch_forefoot_contact_chain
must_move: hindfoot coupling accompanies loaded ankle motion
heel/arch/forefoot contact changes coherently through dorsiflexion and heel rise
toe articulation supports contact rather than penetrating or floating
must_remain_rooted: declared floor-contact zones when contact is required
forbidden_failures: forefoot floating while heel load claimed

exit_rule: No coupling system is accepted from a static pose or endpoint-only evidence. Every required system must have candidate-bound motion evidence showing that all connected attachment neighborhoods respond coherently, with no open Critical/High defect.
